newsitem.title: UK: UK's Graystone sees H2 profits below H1.
newsitem.headline: UK's Graystone sees H2 profits below H1.

text.p: Engineering and distribution group Graystone Plc said on Thursday that current trading indicates that second half profits will be lower than for the first half.
It said in a statement that this reflects a reorganisation being undertaken by a number of its principal customers.
"This has taken longer than had been anticipated, and has resulted in the delay of the launch of certain new products," said Graystone.
Graystone expects pretax profits for the year to June 30, 1997 to exceed eight million stg. The firm made pretax profits of 4.5 million stg in ths six months to December 31, 1996.

The company also announced that talks for the sale of its engineering companies are continuing on schedule. It said the value of offers received so far are in excess of the assets of the businesses being sold and would result in a net cash balance for Graystone if the sale is completed.
Shares in the company fell 11p to 47-1/2 following the announcement, but turnover was slim at just 5,000.
